title: The check prints errors, then warnings, then coverage
statement: `lathe check` MUST print every error, then every warning, then one coverage line per domain and obligation kind, each showing how many are designed, built and proved out of the total." (was "for requirements and for domain rules

title: The check exits non-zero on any error
statement: `lathe check` MUST exit with status 1 when there is at least one error, and with status 0 otherwise. Warnings MUST NOT change the exit status.

title: The check can print each product's whole workspace as structured data
statement: With a machine-readable option, the check MUST print, instead of the text report, structured data listing each product the workspace shows, its folder from the workspace root and its whole workspace.

title: Data that breaks the schema is refused, and is an error
statement: Lathe MUST refuse each record that breaks the schema (a duplicate or malformed ID, an unknown field, a missing title, parent or required field, a parent or link naming a record that does not exist or of a kind it does not allow, a link into another product), and the check MUST report each refusal as a data-refused error naming the file, the line and the rule. An automated test whose file is missing, or does not name the test's ID, MUST be an error naming the test.

title: A data file that does not load is an error, not a crash
statement: A data file that cannot be loaded (a line that is not valid structured data, a value of the wrong type, a record the schema refuses) MUST become data-refused errors naming the file, the line and the rule, and the check MUST report them without crashing. Nothing else MAY be checked until the data loads.

title: Every problem names its check and its record
statement: Every problem MUST name the check that found it and, when it concerns a record, that record's ID, and its message MUST be a plain sentence naming the IDs involved.

title: A test runs at a level its kind allows
statement: A test whose run by level its kind does not allow MUST be reported as a `test-level-not-allowed` warning naming the test, its level and the levels its kind allows (LA-TRC-DS02), and MUST count as proof of nothing (LA-TRC-UC02-R07).

title: A new check needs only a new check record
statement: Adding a check MUST need only a new check, added with the Check aggregate's Add a check command. It MUST NOT need a change to the engine's code.

title: Checks can read every kind of record
statement: A check's query MUST be able to read every kind of record, their parents, links and groups, the scopes, the schema's own definitions, the coverage figures and the product's settings, each with its default when the product has none. Facts about files (whether a test's or a technical record's file exists, and whether a test's file names the test's ID) MUST be filled before the checks run, so a check needs no code of its own.

title: Every check runs, in order, even after one fails
statement: The engine MUST run every check on every load, in the order of LA-CHK-DS01, and MUST collect the problems of all of them in that order, even when one check fails to run.

title: A product's checks run after Lathe's checks
statement: The engine MUST run every check of the product after all of Lathe's checks, in position order, against the same records, and MUST read the same record, message and severity from each. A product with no checks of its own MUST run only Lathe's checks, and a product's check MUST report only on records of its product.

title: A product check's name comes from its record
statement: A product check's problems MUST be named by the check's own name, as Lathe's checks are, whatever its query returns for a name of its own.

title: A product check named like one of Lathe's checks is refused
statement: Lathe MUST refuse a product check whose name one of Lathe's checks has, naming Lathe's shipped checks, so it never runs; the same check written into a data file MUST be a data-refused error.

title: A product check that fails to run is an error naming the check
statement: A product check whose query fails to run MUST be reported as an error under its check name, saying that the check could not run and why, and the other checks MUST still run.

title: The product configuration refuses a checks setting
statement: The product configuration MUST refuse a checks key as an unknown setting, naming it, since a product's checks are records of its data.

title: A record with too many children of one kind is a warning
statement: A record with more children of one kind than the product's `max_children` setting MUST be a `too-many-children` warning that names the record, the kind and the count, and says to add a level between them, such as a capability or another aggregate. The children counted MUST be those of each kind of the five design stages, per kind: a test sits under the one record it proves and is read there, so it is not a child in a list.

title: The limit is the product's max_children setting, 15 by default
statement: The checks MUST read the limit from the product's max_children setting, and use 15 when the product has no settings. Lathe MUST refuse any value that is not a whole number of at least 1.

title: A capability with one child is a warning
statement: A capability with exactly one child MUST be a `lone-child` warning that names it and its child and says to merge it into a neighbor or give it more.

title: A lone child counts the record's own children of every kind
statement: The `lone-child` check MUST count every child of the capability, of any kind, and only its own children, not theirs. A capability with no children, or with two or more, MUST NOT be reported.

title: A flow's steps are counted per path
statement: `too-many-children` MUST count a flow's steps per path (a step with no path is on the main path), since each path reads as its own list, and its message MUST name the path when it is not main.

title: Grouped children are counted per group
statement: `too-many-children` MUST count the children of every kind with a `group_name` (UC requirements, view requirements, API requirements, pattern rules, standard rules and a product's own kinds alike) per `group_name`, read from the store's `record_group` view, the ungrouped ones as one list, with groups compared trimmed and in any letter case, since each group reads under its own heading; its message MUST name the group.

title: A group with one member is a lone child
statement: A group with exactly one member MUST get a `lone-child` warning on its parent, naming the group and its member, as a capability with one child does.

title: An aggregate with too many entities is a warning
statement: An aggregate with more entities than the product's `max_entities_per_aggregate` setting MUST be an `aggregate-too-large` warning that names the aggregate, its count and the limit, and says to split it into smaller aggregates that each change together.

title: The entities limit is the product's setting, 7 by default
statement: The check MUST read the limit from the product's max_entities_per_aggregate setting, and use 7 when the product has no settings. Lathe MUST refuse any value that is not a whole number of at least 1.

title: Every problem of a product shows in one place, as the data is now
statement: Every problem the checks find in one product MUST be shown together, errors before warnings and grouped by check, with the problems that belong to no product, and MUST be shown as the data is after its latest change, without the Owner running a check.

title: A hand edit of a data file is refused and points at the tools
statement: The plugin's guard hook MUST refuse an Agent's Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit of a data file (a structured-data file in the data folder the product configuration names) before it happens, saying to use Lathe's own tools or commands instead.

title: Every other edit goes through silently
statement: The guard hook MUST let an edit of any other file through, with no output.

title: The plugin declares the guard hook and its scripts exist
statement: The plugin MUST declare the guard hook as a PreToolUse hook on Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit, and every script its hooks and MCP server name MUST exist.

title: A write that names technology in the text it sets of an essential record is refused
statement: A command that adds an essential record, or changes its title or lead text, MUST be refused, naming the record and the word, when the text the command sets names technology its kind of record has no business with, as accidental-in-essential reads it: Lathe's words for its kind, the product's own interfaces and its technology words, a term of any of its product's domains still allowed, since a product has one language. Only the text the command sets is read: an add's title and lead text, a change's title or lead text only where it changes them, so a change of one is not refused for a word the other names. A record already in the data is not refused until that text is written; the check keeps reporting every text of it.

title: A write that links an essential record to an accidental one is refused
statement: A command that adds a link from an essential record to an accidental one, or declares a product relation from an essential kind to an accidental kind, MUST be refused, naming both ends: an essential record never points at how it is built, so the link runs from the technical record to what it implements, builds or fills. Only measured_by may, since what measures an outcome may be a report or a script.

title: The essential records are listed alone, by domain
statement: Listing a product's essential records MUST give each of its essential records once, under its domain in position order and those in no domain last, with its kind, title and lead text, and MUST leave out every accidental record and what decides or proves how the product is built: a pattern, its rules and slots, and the tests.

title: Each record is held to the domain-expert test before a change is proposed
statement: Before an Agent proposes adding, changing or removing an essential record, it MUST read the product's essential records as listed and name each one that someone who knows the domain but not software would not recognize or care about, with why, for the Owner to decide; it MUST NOT change an essential record on that finding alone.

title: The Reader finds a record in a domain
statement: The Reader MUST be able to open a domain, find a record in it by its ID or title, and open it.

title: The Reader follows a record's links
statement: From a record's page, the Reader MUST be able to follow any of its links, out or in, to the records at their ends, and back.

title: The Reader walks the model as a graph
statement: The Reader MUST be able to switch to the Graph stage of any page and move through the model by its boxes, from the mouse, the keyboard or touch.

title: The Reader walks the graph through the nav's groups
statement: In the graph, the Reader MUST reach every record through the same stages and kind groups the nav shows, each a place of its own.

title: The Reader reads a record as wiki, graph or model
statement: The Reader MUST be able to open any record at its one address and read it as a wiki page in the wiki card and as a graph, an ERD or a trace on the stage behind it, from the keyboard too.

title: The Reader reads a flow step by step
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read a flow's steps in order on each path, with what each invokes, where it happens and what it fulfills.

title: The Reader moves between products as spaces
statement: The Reader MUST be able to switch between products as spaces, each kept apart, and come back to where they were in each.

title: The rail shows only with two or more products
statement: The space rail MUST show only when the workspace shows two or more products. With one, the nav MUST show no rail and take its width, with the product's name and icon at the top of the nav; collapsed, the nav keeps its controls and lists no spaces.

title: The Reader reads a product in its stage folders
statement: The Reader MUST find a product's records in the nav under Shared and each domain's five stages, as a real product's specs are laid out.

title: The Reader reads the technical specification and test plan by kind
statement: The Reader MUST find a domain's technical records and tests grouped by kind, in the nav, on the domain page and in the graph alike.

title: The Reader explores several places at once in tabs
statement: The Reader MUST be able to explore several places at once, each in a tab of its own with its own focus, stage, view and Back and Forward, open the same record in more than one, and find them all again after a reload.

title: The Reader reads a domain's ERD
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read a domain's model as an ERD of its aggregates, and each aggregate's own, in the ERD stage.

title: The Reader reads a record's history in the wiki card
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read a record's history, the commits that changed its data and what each changed, in the wiki card without leaving the page.

title: The Reader reads a domain's operations and integrations
statement: The Reader MUST be able to find the operation that exposes a command or query, and the flow steps and policies that exchange with an integration.

title: One definition of what changed
statement: What changed MUST be one record diff, the engine's (LA-EXP-QRY13), between the data now and a baseline, by record (its own fields, the parts it owns and the links it starts): each record added, removed, or changed field by field with each value before and after, its parts added, removed or changed, and its links added and removed. Every place that shows a change (the stages' live marks, Highlight changes, the wiki card, the Changes panel and the desktop chat's per-turn diff) MUST use it and MUST NOT diff the data its own way.

title: Live marks on every stage as the data reloads
statement: Each time the data reloads, every stage (the Graph, the ERD and the Trace) MUST mark what the reload changed: an added record a soft glow and a "new" dot, a changed record a brief pulse in its own color then a lasting "changed" dot, a removed record a ghost outline that fades over a few seconds. Under reduced motion it MUST show the dots only, with no glow, pulse or fade.

title: Highlight changes makes every change since a baseline obvious
statement: Highlight changes, a toggle on every stage, MUST make what changed since its baseline obvious, with the stages' one fade and nothing laid out again: every record unchanged MUST dim to about 20%; every changed record MUST carry a pill, text as well as color (New in green, Changed in amber, Removed in red), a thick outline in its color and a light tint, all kept while Highlight changes is on; a removed record MUST stay as a dashed ghost box, not fading, until Highlight changes is turned off; and a pill MUST be left out below a readable size, the container's roll-up (LA-EXP-UC15-R07) carrying the change there. Its baseline picker MUST offer since the last commit (the default), since the branch left main (the merge base with the default branch) and since I last looked, which is kept per product per Reader in the session setting and moved to now when the Reader turns Highlight changes off or leaves the product.

title: The diff shows in the wiki card
statement: The wiki card of a record changed since the baseline MUST show what changed, per field and link: each changed field old → new, each part added, removed or changed, and the links added and removed listed. An added record's card MUST say "New since <baseline>".

title: Follow glides to each change as it lands
statement: Follow, off by default, MUST glide the camera to each change as it lands. Any camera move or focus by the Reader MUST turn it off, with a note saying so.

title: The Changes panel lists the changes
statement: A Changes panel over the stage MUST list the changes newest first, by record, each a card; clicking one MUST focus its record on the stage. Its toggle MUST show how many records changed.

title: Every container rolls up its changes
statement: With Highlight changes on, every container (a domain, a stage, a folder, an aggregate) MUST show on its box how many records under it are new, changed and removed ("3 new · 5 changed · 1 removed", leaving out what is zero), and the nav MUST show the counts beside each domain, stage and folder, so changes are findable when zoomed out. A removed record has no box and MUST count under the nearest container its ID names.

title: Changes out of view are marked and pointed to
statement: With Highlight changes on, the minimap MUST mark each changed record, and each edge of a stage MUST show a hint counting the changes past it ("4 changes →").

title: Next change and Previous change walk the changes
statement: The commands Next change and Previous change, bound to ] and [ by default and rebindable through Key bindings, MUST move the stage's focus to the next or previous new or changed record in reading order (ID order), around at the ends, and announce each step and its place in the walk.

title: The Reader reads a journey step by step
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read a journey's steps in order on each path, the main path first, with what each carries out, who acts and where it sits, and see where the acting role changes.

title: A use case or policy names the journeys it is a step of
statement: A use case's and a policy's page MUST name each journey it is a step of, with the step, its path and position and the steps before and after it, each a link.

title: In the graph a journey's steps sit under it in order
statement: In the graph a journey's steps MUST sit under it, in order on each path, each linked to what it carries out.

title: The Reader's choice of how the graph is drawn lasts the session
statement: The Reader MUST be able to choose the graph's layout, the minimap and, in the Map, all links, from the graph itself, and the choice MUST hold for every page and tab of the window for the rest of the session, until they change it.

title: A view exists because it presents commands and queries
statement: A view MUST have no owner, its product following from its ID, and one that presents no command or query MUST be reported as an error.

title: A view rule is a view requirement
statement: A rule of a view MUST be a view requirement under its view, proved by its view tests.

title: An endpoint exposes one command or query
statement: An endpoint MUST sit under the one command or query it exposes, and a flow step MUST reach it through that command or query, never directly.

title: An endpoint rule is an API requirement
statement: A rule of an endpoint MUST be an API requirement under its endpoint, proved by its endpoint tests.

title: An integration exists because steps or policies exchange with it
statement: An integration MUST have no owner, its product following from its ID, and one that no flow step or policy exchanges with MUST be reported as an error.

title: A UI component renders views, and one that renders none is an error
statement: A UI component MUST sit under its domain, name its file, link each view it renders with `renders` and each view requirement its code does with `builds`; one that renders no view MUST be reported as an error naming it, whose message says to use it or remove it.

title: The reference says what a domain is
statement: The domain table's description in the schema, shown in the reference, MUST say that a domain is for one business capability, and the `domain-named-for-technology` check's explanation MUST say that a domain is a vertical slice of business capability whose technology is written as the technical records that implement its design.

title: The modeling skill finds the capabilities first
statement: The plugin's modeling skill MUST start, before any record is written, by finding the product's business capabilities and making each one a domain, and MUST list the questions that tell a capability from a technology layer.

title: Each domain says its subdomain type
statement: Each domain MUST say its subdomain type: core for the product's edge, supporting or generic, which guides how much modeling it deserves.

title: Every use case sits under a capability with a whole-number position
statement: A capability MUST sit under a domain and give its place in a required `position`. Every use case MUST sit under one of its domain's capabilities.

title: A repository persists one aggregate
statement: A repository MUST persist exactly one aggregate, and an aggregate MUST have exactly one repository. Code that keeps several aggregates splits into one repository each; an aggregate no repository persists is an `aggregate-without-repository` gap.

title: Domain services and terms are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have `domain_service` under a domain, which its commands and queries `calls`, and `term` under a domain for its glossary.

title: Capabilities and journeys serve outcomes, many to many
statement: A capability or a journey MAY serve any number of its product's business outcomes, and an outcome MAY be served by any number of capabilities and journeys, each a serves link from the capability or journey; only a capability or a journey serves, and only an outcome is served.

title: A record moved to another domain takes that domain's IDs
statement: Moving a record that sits in a domain (a capability, term, domain service, repository, aggregate, read model, specification, test data set, table, entry point, tooling, data store, open question, or a record of a product's own kind) to another domain of its product MUST give it, and every record under it whose ID starts with the old domain's, the new domain's ID in its place, the rest of each ID kept, and MUST carry each new ID into every record that names the old one, in its fields, its links and its text, so nothing names an ID that is gone. A domain of another product, or a new ID another record already has, MUST be refused.

title: The Owner puts a product's domains in order
statement: Each domain MUST have a position among its product's domains, from 1 and its own within the product, which the Owner gives when adding the domain and changes with Change a domain; every list of a product's domains (the nav, the product page, the Graph and the reports) MUST show them by position, never by ID.

title: Entities, their fields and invariants are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have the entity under an aggregate, with its role and its fields, `has_one` and `has_many` from entity to entity, and the invariant under an aggregate with its statement. The reference MUST describe them.

title: An entity has its fields, in order
statement: Each entity MUST have its fields in order, each with a name, a meaning, exactly one type, whether it is required, and an example when it helps. An entity, event or read model with no fields MUST be reported as a gap.

title: Another aggregate is referenced by ID, through a field
statement: A reference to another aggregate MUST be a field typed by that aggregate. In its own domain its table MAY hold a foreign key; a foreign key MUST NOT point into another domain, where the reference stays a plain ID.

title: Uniqueness is an invariant its rule enforces
statement: A rule that no two records share a value MUST be an invariant, enforced by its rule; a unique key that backs it up MUST name it.

title: A child entity its root does not reach is an entity-unreferenced warning
statement: Each child entity SHOULD be reached from its aggregate's root by `has_one` or `has_many` links inside the aggregate. One that is not MUST be reported as an `entity-unreferenced` warning naming it and its root; an aggregate without exactly one root MUST NOT have its children judged.

title: Commands and policies are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have `command` under the entity it changes with `raises` and `checks`, and `policy` under the command it invokes with `hears` and `exchanges_with`, the link a flow step also has to an integration. The reference MUST describe them.

title: A command changes only its own aggregate
statement: A command MUST change exactly its own aggregate: the one the entity it sits under belongs to, and no other. Where a change seems to reach another aggregate, the model changes: the other aggregate reacts to an event through a policy, or the two are one aggregate.

title: A policy names the integrations it exchanges with
statement: A policy MAY name the integrations of its product it exchanges with as it acts, such as the mail service a reminder is sent through, written with Add a policy or Change a policy and read with its command.

title: Specifications are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have `specification` with no owner, reading one or more aggregates of one domain with `reads`, which commands `checks` and queries `selects_by`, with a required statement.

title: A specification nothing uses is an error
statement: A specification that no command checks and no query selects by MUST be reported as an error naming it, whose message says to use it or remove it.

title: Read models and queries are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have `read_model` under a domain with its fields and `reads`, and `query` under the one read model it reads.

title: Value objects and their constraints are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have value objects with no owner, their fields, and constraints under them, each with a required statement. The reference MUST describe them.

title: A value object nothing uses is an error
statement: A value object that no entity, event or read model field is typed by MUST be reported as an error naming it, whose message says to use it or remove it.

title: Domain events are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have a domain event under an aggregate, with whether it is published, its event fields and its event type. The reference MUST describe them.

title: An event has its fields, as an entity does
statement: The engine MUST give each domain event its fields. An event with no fields MUST be reported as a gap, and the store MUST refuse a field without a name, or named twice.

title: An event a policy hears is delivered by outbox
statement: An event a policy hears, whose aggregate is stored in a table, and whose event type does not give `outbox` as its delivery MUST be reported as an `event-not-by-outbox` warning naming the event and its policies. An event that only keeps read models current (fed_by), where those read models are rebuilt from the data on every load, MAY be delivered in process, and MUST NOT be reported, whether it is published or not.

title: Storage requirements are obligations under an aggregate or read model
statement: The schema MUST have `storage_requirement`, an obligation under exactly one aggregate or read model with a required statement, and `storage_requirement_test` under it; coverage MUST count it designed by construction, built only when its aggregate's repository or its read model's reader names a file that exists and its data store, and proved by one of its tests.

title: loadWorkspace returns the Workspace contract
statement: Loading a product's workspace MUST return the Workspace read model: every product's records, links, problems and coverage. Fields MAY be added to it but MUST NOT be renamed or removed.

title: Loading is fast enough to reload live
statement: loadWorkspace(root) MUST load Lathe's own spec in under 2 s, and load it again after one record changes in under 500 ms, on the dev machine, as the performance script (npm --prefix lathe run test:perf) measures, so the Workbench and an Agent's script can reload on every write. Every check still runs on every load. When the machine is busy (a one-minute load average above 12) the script measures but judges nothing, and a budget is never loosened. It MAY take timings in its options, which it fills with how long each phase took (open, files, checks, coverage, total).

title: Each load reads the data files afresh and writes nothing
statement: Each load MUST read the data files afresh, Lathe's own checks beside the product's, into a new in-memory store. The engine MUST NOT write the data to a storage file or keep it between loads, so the data files stay the only source of truth; the one storage file it keeps is the schema cache, which holds the migrated schema and never a product's data (LA-PLT-UC01-R11), and beside it the validated-build stamps, which hold a key and never a product's data (LA-PLT-UC01-R17). It MAY keep the reference while no file in the data folders or the schema has changed.

title: A command answers within a budget
statement: The engine MUST start fast enough that a cold command, lathe use-case get-use-case --id <id> on Lathe's own spec run in a fresh process, finishes in under 800 ms on the dev machine, as the performance script (npm --prefix lathe run test:perf) measures, so an Agent can run one command per step, and the Agent tool server (which starts the same engine) answers its first call, without waiting on the engine's start-up; when the machine is busy (a one-minute load average above 12) the script measures but judges nothing, and the budget is never loosened.

title: The schema is cached, never the data, and a bad cache is never used
statement: The engine MUST start from a cached copy of the migrated schema (Lathe's, and a product's with its own kinds and relations) when there is one, and otherwise build it and cache it, one DuckDB file per schema in .cache/lathe of the node_modules folder that holds Lathe (or LATHE_CACHE_DIR), never in a product's files and never with a product's data; each file MUST be keyed by a hash of Lathe's and DuckDB's versions, the migrations, the engine's code and the product's declarations, and stamped with that key inside it, so a file whose stamp names another key, or that does not open, is never used and the schema is built afresh and cached again; a file MUST be written under a name of its own and renamed into place, so two processes that start at once never read half of one; and the cache MUST keep only the current base schema's files, and at most the 20 products' schemas written last.

title: Files a whole build passed are not built again
statement: When a load's whole build passes (every key, check, integrity query and aggregate rule), the engine MUST record a validated-build stamp beside the schema cache (LA-PLT-UC01-R11), keyed by a hash of each data file's folder, name and exact contents, the base schema's key and every file of the engine's code; a later load whose key has a stamp MUST read the files' records without building them again, and build the store only when a query first needs it. The stamp MUST hold its key alone and never a product's data. A load of files whose key has no stamp, or whose stamp names another key, MUST be built whole, so a command MUST answer and refuse exactly as the whole build does; and the cache MUST keep at most the 50 stamps of the current base schema written last.

title: Init writes a config and a first product record
statement: lathe init --name <name> --prefix <prefix> MUST write the product's config file with this Lathe's schema version when the repo has none, and MUST add the product record with that ID and title to the product's data file through the store. It MUST refuse a prefix that is not a valid ID and MUST NOT overwrite an existing product record.

title: The product's config names its data folder
statement: Every command MUST read the data folder from the data setting of the product's config file, defaulting to data, and MUST NOT read records from any other folder. A setting the config does not define MUST be refused with an error that names it.

title: A product adds its own kinds without forking Lathe
statement: A product's own kinds and relations MUST be records of the kinds product kind, product kind field and product relation in its own data, which add kinds to the schema for that product only. They MUST NOT widen one of Lathe's kinds; that takes a migration.

title: Each clone sets up the merge driver for the data files
statement: A product repo's .gitattributes MUST name its data files for the lathe-data merge driver, and the README MUST say how each clone sets it up once with git config merge.lathe-data.name and git config merge.lathe-data.driver "npx lathe merge-data %O %A %B %P", so two branches' new records merge record by record instead of clashing line by line.

title: The product's config names its test files
statement: The tests setting of the product's config file MUST list globs, relative to the product root, of the files that hold its test cases, defaulting to **/*.test.{ts,tsx,js,mjs} and **/*.spec.{ts,tsx,js}. Whatever the globs, files in node_modules, dist or a folder with its own config file MUST NOT be read. A tests value that is not a non-empty list of globs MUST be refused, naming the setting.

title: A workspace lists the other products it shows
statement: The products setting of a workspace's config file MUST list the folders, relative to its root, of the other products it shows, each holding its own config file and data. Each MUST load beside the workspace's own product from its own folder, with its own config, schema version check, checks, tracing and coverage, as its own space. A listed folder that is the workspace itself, is listed twice or holds no config file, a listed product that lists products of its own, and one product ID in two products' folders MUST be refused with an error that names it.

title: lathe check checks every product of the workspace
statement: `lathe check` at a workspace MUST check every product it shows, each in its own folder, and report each on its own (its errors, warnings and coverage, then its counts), then the counts of them all. It MUST exit 1 when any product has an error.

title: A folder with its own config is another product's, never the workspace's
statement: Tracing MUST treat a folder with its own config file as another product's: the workspace's source files, test files, router files and default package folders MUST NOT include a file in it, and a package folder the workspace's config lists inside it MUST be refused, naming it.

title: Views reload when any product's data files or Lathe's checks change
statement: When a file in the data folder of any product the workspace shows, or one of Lathe's own checks or migrations, changes, the server SHOULD send spec:changed, and the open view SHOULD then load the data again without a manual refresh, staying at the same address.

title: A view reads again only what a change touched
statement: The server MUST announce each change (Data files changed) with the kinds whose records it changed and the read models built from one of them, or every read model when the data loaded afresh or was refused; an open view MUST then read again only the reads of the read models named. After its own write, the view MUST wait for the server's change for that write, which the server sends before it answers, and read everything again only when no change comes within 300 ms or no channel is open.

title: A change reloads only the kinds it changed
statement: When data files change, the store MUST read again only the changed files' kinds, a change set from one write or a burst of writes being one reload, and hold them at once to the keys (each record's foreign keys, every record pointing into them, their unique keys, every ID once across kinds) and to the rules of each aggregate whose rules read a changed kind; it MUST build again only the read models built from a changed kind. The rest of the whole build (the store's checks, the integrity queries and every aggregate's rules) MUST then run in the background, and data it refuses MUST be refused. A reload and a load from scratch of the same files MUST give the same records on the same lines, the same refusal, the same reads and the same problems, coverage and chains. A changed declaration of the product's own kinds or relations, or a file of no kind, MUST load every file afresh.

title: The checks run in the background after a burst of changes
statement: After a change to the data, by a command or by anything else, the server MUST run the checks and coverage in the background on the data built whole, 150 ms after the last change and the last request on the data have answered, so that a burst of changes (a git pull, an Agent's writes) makes one run and the reads a change sets off (a view reading again what changed) answer before the run holds the server, though never more than 1 s after the change; it MUST answer the problems and coverage from the last run meanwhile, and MUST announce the checks' read models when the run is ready. A command still refuses on its aggregate's rules before saving, and its commit MUST refuse whatever the data's whole build would refuse: it holds the new state to the keys and the rules of each aggregate that reads a changed kind, then, over the data last built whole with the kinds that differ beside it, to those records' field constraints and every integrity query, building the data whole only when the command changes the product's kinds or relations or something is refused, so that the whole build follows in the background as after a reload.

title: A large product stays within its budgets
statement: On the large product (LA-PLT-TD04, about ten times Lathe's records), served as lathe serve serves it on the dev machine, one edit to a data file MUST be visible in under 500 ms from the file's change (the reload, the rules it reruns and the reads the change names, read again), and so MUST one of the Workbench's own writes from its request (the command's commit and the same reads); the checks' run after it MUST be announced within 4 s of the change; and a cold load with every check MUST take under 4 s, as the performance script (npm --prefix lathe run test:perf) measures. The budgets are never loosened to make a run pass.

title: The Reader arranges the workbench and it stays so
statement: The Reader MUST be able to resize, hide and bring back the panels of the workbench, by pointer or keyboard, and find them as they left them.

title: The Reader chooses or makes a theme for the whole app
statement: The Reader MUST be able to choose a theme and a color mode that apply to the whole app at once, make, share and import a theme of their own, and choose whether scroll zooms the stages or pans them.

title: Open Product Folder picks a folder and opens it in its own window
statement: File › Open Product Folder… (Cmd+O, Ctrl+O elsewhere) MUST let the reader choose a folder and open it in a window of its own. A folder that is not a product MUST be refused with a message saying what is missing.

title: The window names the product and its folder
statement: The window's title MUST be the names of the products in the folder (the titles of their product records, joined by commas), then the folder, with the home folder shown as ~. The Workbench MUST NOT change it.

title: A window opens with the shell background, with no white flash
statement: A window MUST stay hidden until its content is ready to show, and its background MUST be the Workbench's shell color (--shell) for the system's light or dark appearance, so it never flashes white.

title: The Workbench reaches the shell only through window.latheDesktop
statement: Every window MUST run the Workbench with context isolation and the sandbox on and Node integration off. The preload MUST expose only window.latheDesktop with isDesktop, platform, onCommand and setChrome, and nothing of Node or Electron.

title: Links that leave the app open in the system browser
statement: A link to any other origin than the window's own server MUST open in the system browser, and the window MUST NOT navigate away from Lathe or open windows of its own.

title: Quitting waits for every window's server to stop
statement: When the app quits, also when it is stopped from a terminal, it MUST wait until the server of every window, closed ones included, has stopped before the process exits, so it always exits cleanly even while a reload is in progress, and MUST give up waiting after 10 seconds so a server that hangs cannot keep it from quitting.

title: A workspace opens with every product it lists
statement: Opening a workspace's folder MUST show every product its config file lists, beside its own, in the one window; the title MUST name them all, and a record's data file MUST be found in its own product's data folder.

title: A Product window opens a product with its own installed Lathe
statement: A Product window MUST be served by the product's own built Lathe (node_modules/@jaredrob/lathe) when it has one, and by the bundled copy otherwise, and its About window MUST say which, with the version, for the product in front.

title: The app remembers the recent folders and each window's place
statement: File › Open Recent MUST list the folders opened last and reopen one; the next launch MUST reopen the last folder; and a window MUST keep its size and place when it moves, resizes or closes, and reopen there.

title: Development loads the 5199 dev server when it serves the opened folder
statement: In development a window MUST load the local dev server on port 5199 when that server answers for the opened folder, so changes hot-reload exactly as in the browser.

title: Otherwise the shell starts a dev server of its own for the folder
statement: When 5199 does not answer, or answers for another folder, the shell MUST start the app's Vite dev server on a free port with `LATHE_ROOT` set to the opened folder, and load it. The dev API plugin MUST read its product folder from `LATHE_ROOT`, defaulting to Lathe's own repo, so the owner's 5199 server is unchanged.

title: A change to the main process or preload restarts Electron
statement: A change to a file of the shell MUST rebuild the shell and restart Electron. A build that fails MUST leave the running shell as it is.

title: Record changes reload the view in every mode
statement: A change to the opened product's specs MUST reload what the window shows, whether it loads from serve(), the shell's own dev server or the 5199 server.

title: A local build is unsigned and stays on this Mac
statement: A local build MUST build Lathe first, then an unsigned macOS app for this Mac's architecture, in a folder git ignores. It MUST NOT sign, notarize, publish or add auto-update.

title: The Workbench writes through each command's own operation
statement: The Workbench MUST change data only by sending one command's fields to that command's own operation on the App server, which MUST run it in its own transaction and answer with the records it changed, or with a refusal (status 422) that carries every reason.

title: Only the Workbench's own views can write
statement: The server MUST refuse a command that comes from another site's view, that is not structured data, or whose body is over 1 MB, before the command runs.

title: Lathe loads only data for its own schema version
statement: Every load, from any of Lathe's interfaces (including loadWorkspace and openStore), MUST stop, reading no data, when the product's config file names another schema version than Lathe's, with one message: for an older one "This product's data is for schema N; this Lathe uses schema M. Run `npx lathe upgrade` to move it forward.", for a newer one that it needs a newer Lathe: update @jaredrob/lathe. A config with no schema version MUST be read as version 1, and one that is not a whole number from 1 MUST be refused.

title: Upgrade converts the data in order and loads it
statement: lathe upgrade MUST run the converters in lathe/upgrades/ in order from the product's schema version to Lathe's, each on the raw records of the data files. Only once the converted data loads under the new schema, with every aggregate's rules, MUST it raise the config's schema version, and print what each converter changed. It MUST refuse when a converter is missing, and MUST NOT keep or read the old form afterwards.

title: Upgrade lists what it could not convert
statement: What a converter cannot convert MUST be printed as a to-do list for the Owner, never dropped. When the converted data does not load, the upgrade MUST stop without raising the schema version and list the store's refusals as the to-dos.

title: Upgrade refuses a working tree with changes
statement: `lathe upgrade` MUST refuse, changing nothing, when the product's git working tree has changes or the product is not under git, so the upgrade is one reviewable commit.

title: The plugin warns once when its skills are for another major version
statement: The plugin's MCP launcher MUST read the product's installed Lathe version and schema version, and when the installed major version is not the one the plugin's manifest says its skills were written for (`lathe.major`), MUST add one warning naming both to the first tool result, and to no other.

title: Outside a Lathe repo the launcher says why it cannot start
statement: When the folder Claude Code runs in holds no Lathe repo, the plugin's MCP launcher MUST say why it cannot start, and start nothing.

title: A command takes its fields as structured data from any interface
statement: Every command MUST take its fields as one structured object in the same shape from any of Lathe's interfaces, read by one reader, with text kept exactly as given and the same validation and refusals as its separate field values; giving the object together with separate field values MUST be refused as bad usage, and the result MUST be printed as structured data.

title: The plugin's skills write only through the tools
statement: The plugin's skills MUST tell the Agent to change data only through the aggregates' tools or commands, never by editing data files. They MUST NOT restate what the tools, refusals and lathe/REFERENCE.md already say (kinds, ID patterns, tool names): each points to the reference once, and keeps only the judgment the tools cannot teach.

title: The Owner talks with their own Claude Code
statement: In a Product window, the Owner MUST be able to talk with their own Claude Code, run in the product folder with their login and settings, in a chat panel beside the stage, and never through an API key or an agent loop of Lathe's own.

title: Claude's answers link the records they name
statement: Claude's answers MUST read as rich text, and a record ID in them MUST open that record on the stage.

title: Claude's work shows as tool entries and record diffs
statement: Each tool call Claude makes MUST show as a compact entry that expands to its input and result, and the records the spec gained, lost or changed during a turn MUST show by record, from the one record diff (LA-EXP-QRY13) of the spec before the turn against the spec after it.

title: The Owner answers permission prompts and stops a turn
statement: A tool call that needs the Owner's permission MUST wait for their answer in the chat (allow once or deny), and the Owner MUST be able to stop the turn under way.

title: The Owner resumes, forks or starts a session
statement: The Owner MUST be able to resume or fork any of the folder's saved Claude Code sessions, listed by title and date, or start a new one, and MUST be warned, with a fork offered, when the session may be open in another Claude client.

title: Every chat brings Lathe's own tools
statement: Every chat session a Product window starts MUST load the Lathe plugin of the Lathe the window runs (the product's own installed Lathe's, else the bundled copy's), its tools running that same Lathe whatever the Owner has installed, and MUST list each Lathe tool once when the Owner has the plugin installed too.

title: The Owner chooses what Claude may do without asking
statement: The Owner MUST be able to choose the chat's permission mode in one control: Ask (every tool asks, reads included), Accept reads (the default: reads run without asking, everything else asks), Auto (Claude Code's auto mode decides), Bypass (nothing asks; turned on only after a warning, and marked while on) or View only (only reads: every Lathe command, and every tool that writes files or runs code, is withheld or refused, the refusal saying the chat is View only). A new chat MUST start in the mode the folder's last chat had.

title: The chat says what it runs with
statement: The chat MUST show how many Lathe tools the session has and from which Lathe, and when `claude` is not found or not signed in MUST say so with the fix (where to install it, or `/login`) before the first message, instead of failing on it.

title: A tool can be allowed for the rest of the chat
statement: A permission prompt MUST offer to allow its tool always in this chat, after which that tool MUST run without asking for the rest of the chat; View only's refusals still hold.

title: Claude knows where the Owner is
statement: Each message MUST carry, as context apart from the Owner's own words, what they are looking at in the window (the product, the view, the stage, the focused record and the selection), shown as a chip above the message box that they can remove; Claude MUST be told to start from it, and to use app_focus and app_open, never a search of the code, for anything else about the window.

title: The Owner dictates a message, recognized on the Mac
statement: Where the Mac can recognize speech on-device, the Owner MUST be able to dictate a message from the mic control or its rebindable key, its words appearing in the message box as they speak, to edit before sending; the audio MUST NOT leave the Mac nor be recorded or saved, the Owner MUST be told so before macOS first asks for the microphone, and where on-device recognition is not available the mic MUST be hidden.

title: Claude's changes can be reviewed on the stage
statement: After a turn that changed the spec, the Owner MUST be able to put the turn's changed records under review: the stage MUST light those records alone, as Highlight changes does, and next and previous change MUST walk through them, each with its diff.

title: A record ID in a reply opens in a new tab on request
statement: A record ID in Claude's reply MUST focus the stage when chosen plainly and open the record in a new tab when chosen with Cmd or Ctrl held or with the mouse's middle control.

title: The Owner points at a record and asks Claude about it
statement: The Owner MUST be able to attach the box they point at on any stage to their message (Ask Claude About This in the record's menu, and a key), each shown above the message box as a chip with the record's ID and title that they can take out, and sent as context beside what they are looking at; boxes pointed at one after another MUST all stay attached until the message is sent.

title: Typing a slash lists the skills and commands
statement: Typing a slash at the start of the message box MUST list the skills and slash commands Claude Code finds for the folder (the Owner's, the folder's, the installed plugins' and Lathe's, and its own that work without a dialog), each with a one-line description, narrowed by the name typed and picked by keyboard or pointer.

title: The Owner chooses the model and the effort
statement: The Owner MUST be able to choose the model (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku or Claude Code's default) and the effort in the chat's head, the conversation continuing on the same session with them, and the control MUST NOT change them while Claude works.

title: Messages typed while Claude works are queued
statement: While Claude works, the chat MUST show Stop (and Escape stops), and a message the Owner sends MUST be queued, listed above the message box and sent in order as each turn ends, each removable until it goes.

title: Images go with a message
statement: The Owner MUST be able to paste images and screenshots into a message and send the stage as it is drawn as an image; the images MUST go with the message as thumbnails they can take out first, at most six of at most 5 MB each of the types Claude Code reads, and any other file MUST be refused saying why.

title: Serve needs no build tools in the product repo
statement: lathe serve MUST serve the Workbench and its operations for the product repo, and every other product its config lists, from the installed package alone, and open views MUST reload when any of their data files change.

title: A stopped server leaves no storage work running
statement: Stopping a server that serve() started MUST stop its watchers and take no more requests, MUST wait for any load, reload or write in progress and for the engine's background work, and MUST close its stores and, once no store in the process is open, the storage engine before it resolves, so a process that exits then exits cleanly; lathe serve MUST stop this way on SIGINT and SIGTERM and then end by that signal.

title: Serve shows every product and writes to each one's own folder
statement: lathe serve, the Workbench's dev server and the Product window MUST serve every product the workspace shows, each as its own space, with each record's file and line in its own product's folder. A write MUST go to the data folder of the product whose records its commands name (a write that names none, such as a new product's, to the workspace's own), and a write that names records of two products MUST be refused with the reason.

title: Serve opens to the local network only when asked
statement: The served spec MUST be reachable from this machine alone unless the Owner asks for the local network when starting the server, and then MUST also be reachable from other devices on the same network, such as a phone on the same Wi-Fi, and MUST tell the Owner each address those devices open.

title: Other devices on the network read; only this machine writes
statement: Because the local network has no sign-in, a change to the spec MUST be refused, with the reason in the Owner's words, when it comes from any device but the machine Lathe runs on, while that device MUST still be able to read the spec and MUST be told it reads only.

title: A shortcut's new keys show everywhere at once
statement: The Reader MUST be able to bind a key to a shortcut, remove one, reset a shortcut to its own keys and, after being asked, reset every shortcut, and the palette, the sheet, every tooltip and what assistive technology announces MUST show the change at once and after a reload.

title: A record's data file opens where the Owner chose
statement: From a record the Owner MUST be able to reveal its data file in Finder, open it in the editor they chose or their own command, and copy its ID; the shell MUST take only the record's ID and find the file itself.

title: Voice activation wakes the chat, and commands act on the draft
statement: With voice activation on, "Lathe" (or the wake phrase chosen) said after a pause MUST open the message box and start dictating, the rest of the utterance becoming the message, and MUST NOT wake the chat mid-sentence; while dictating, a pause, the wake phrase and a command word ending the utterance MUST send, clear, remove the last sentence or start a paragraph, and any other words MUST stay text; about 20 seconds of quiet MUST end dictation and leave the draft.

title: The chat listens only in front, and only when asked
statement: Voice activation MUST be off until the Owner turns it on, and the chat MUST listen only while its window is in front: going behind another window or app stops listening and leaves the draft.

title: Quick mode sends when the Owner has finished
statement: With Quick mode on, a dictated message MUST be sent by itself after a pause judged on the Mac from the words and the voice's pitch: about half a second after a finished thought, 3 to 4 seconds mid-thought and about 2 seconds when unsure, or a fixed 2 seconds where the voice cannot be read; a countdown MUST show on Send, and any sound or key MUST cancel it.

title: A turn can be undone in one step
statement: The Owner MUST be able to undo a turn's changes to the spec in one step, made through the aggregates' own commands in reverse as one write, and the undo MUST be refused, with every reason and nothing changed, when something since depends on what the turn made or the records changed again after the turn; it MUST NOT edit files or reset git.

title: Clearing the recent folders empties every list of them
statement: Clearing the recent folders MUST empty File › Open Recent and the Dock menu's list, and the next folder opened MUST be the only one listed.

title: Claude sees the Reader's focus and opens records
statement: Claude MUST be able to ask what the Reader is looking at (the focused record, the stage and the selection) and to open a record in the window, and both MUST refuse when no app window is connected.

title: Claude reaches the window from a shell too
statement: Lathe's commands MUST offer what the Agent's app tools do, lathe app focus and lathe app open <id> [--stage graph|erd|trace], through the same bridge and the same code, refusing with exit 1 when no Product window is connected.

title: A schema change takes effect on the next load
statement: A changed migration MUST take effect on the next load with no other code change: the store applies the migrations in order, records them, and reads the schema back from what it built. That is rebuilt from the data files, so there are no upgrade migrations.

title: Existing data is checked against the changed schema
statement: After a schema change, every product's data MUST be loaded against the new schema, so that a change which breaks existing data shows as `data-refused` errors straight away, and a change that would leave records without a table is refused.

title: The record types and the reference follow the schema
statement: The record types and the committed reference MUST be generated from the schema, and a test MUST fail when either differs from what the schema gives.

title: Kinds and relations are the schema, not code
statement: Every kind and every relation MUST be defined by the schema's numbered migrations or generated from a product's declarations. The engine, the checks and the app MUST NOT hard-code the list of kinds or relations.

title: Lathe's schema changes only by a migration
statement: Lathe's own kinds, fields and relations MUST change only by a new numbered migration, reviewed in git. The app, the API and the aggregates' commands MUST NOT change the schema: no command writes a meta table.

title: Obligations and link roles come only from the schema
statement: Which kinds are obligations MUST come only from each kind's `obligation` flag in the schema, and a product's own obligation kinds MUST be designed and proved only by links of relations whose role is design or proof.

title: Every table, field, kind and relation of Lathe's is described
statement: Lathe's tables, fields, kinds and relations MUST each have a description, as comments in its migrations, and every check its summary and explanation.

title: A breaking schema change raises the schema version and brings a converter
statement: Lathe's schema version MUST be one whole number, kept only in the schema's version file and starting at 1. A schema change that existing data may not pass (a renamed or removed table or field, a new required field, a narrower rule) MUST raise it by one, MUST add the converter `lathe/upgrades/<from>-to-<to>.ts` that moves the data forward exactly one version, and MUST raise the package's major version; a change every existing product still passes MUST NOT.

title: Each test sits under what it tests, as that thing's test kind
statement: Each test MUST be of the test kind named after what it tests or its owner, and sit under that one record, the only obligation it proves.

title: A product kind gets a table of its own
statement: A product kind MUST give the product a table named after the kind, with an ID, a title, a required reference to its parent kind and a stored field for each of its fields, typed and required as declared; an obligation kind MUST join the obligation supertype.

title: A product kind keeps its own label, stage and obligation
statement: A product kind MUST be listed after Lathe's kinds, with its own label, stage and obligation, in any of the six stages or none, and MUST NOT change any of Lathe's kinds.

title: A product relation adds a link table or a pair
statement: A product_relation with a new name MUST get a link table of its own; one with Lathe's name MUST add only its pair, and MUST change nothing else of that relation.

title: A kind declared twice is refused, naming its file and line
statement: Two product kinds with the same name MUST be refused by the store, naming the file and line of the second and the line of the first.

title: A product relation declared twice is refused, naming the file and line
statement: The store MUST refuse a product relation with the same name, source kind and target kind as another, once, naming its file and line.

title: A product's own interaction design kind presents commands and queries, as a view does
statement: A product MAY let a kind of its own whose stage is interaction design present commands and queries, by a product relation named presents from that kind to command or to query, so one record (an invocation) presents several commands and queries of any of the product's domains, as a view does; a product relation named presents from any other kind MUST be refused.

title: The engine loads the stages and each kind's stage and position
statement: The engine MUST load the stages in order and each kind's stage and position from the schema. The product and open questions MUST sit outside the stages.

title: A product places its own kinds in a stage
statement: A product kind MAY name one of the six stages, or none, and MUST NOT add a stage or change one of Lathe's kinds.

title: Kinds are read in one order, the schema's
statement: Every list of kinds, in the app, the reference and coverage, MUST read them in one order: Lathe's kinds by their position in the schema (the product, then stage by stage, each kind by its position, then open questions), then a product's own kinds by name. No code MAY keep a list of its own.

title: The reference script prints the reference, or writes it to a file
statement: The reference MUST be written as Markdown: how data is kept, then the kinds with their tables, the other tables, the relations, the stages and the checks, each with its own anchor. The Owner MUST be able to print it or write it to a file of their choosing.

title: The reference gives every fact of each kind, table, relation, stage and check
statement: The reference MUST give each kind's label, description, stage, parents and children, obligation (yes or no), ID pattern and ID scope; each table's role, keys and fields with their types, values, references and descriptions; each relation's role, labels, description and pairs; each stage's position, label and description; and each check's name, severity, summary, explanation and kinds. The engine's own problem, `data-refused`, MUST be listed as a check too, and the reference MUST say that clean architecture's use case is a command handler in Lathe.

title: A product's reference shows its own kinds and its own checks
statement: The reference MUST be the product's own: its kinds, tables and relations with its declarations, and its own checks after Lathe's and the engine's.

title: Lathe's committed reference never goes stale
statement: Lathe's reference MUST be committed as `lathe/REFERENCE.md`, so an agent can read it without running anything. The package build MUST regenerate it, and a test MUST fail when the committed file differs from what the reference script writes. It is generated from the schema and the checks, never written by hand.

title: What the reference would leave blank is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a product kind or relation without a description, and a check without its summary or explanation; Lathe's own tables, kinds and checks MUST all be described.

title: Relations read in plain words from both ends
statement: Each relation MUST carry a `forward_label`, the link read from its source ("Raises"), and a `reverse_label`, the link read from its target ("Raised by"), in sentence case. The reference MUST show both and list each kind's links out by their forward labels and its links in by their reverse labels. The store MUST refuse a product relation without both.

title: A kind or check met while reading opens its reference in one step
statement: Wherever the Reader meets a kind or a check while reading the spec (a record's kind, a problem's code, a field), they MUST be able to open what the reference says about it in one step, without leaving the workbench.

title: Both sides' records are kept, sorted
statement: The merge driver MUST keep the records each side added, and a change or a removal made on one side only, keep one copy of a record both sides added alike, and write the merged file sorted by key.

title: A real clash fails the merge, naming it
statement: The merge driver MUST fail, exiting 1 and naming the clash, when one key is added on both sides with different content, or one record is changed on both sides or removed on one and changed on the other.

title: The merged table's own rules are checked
statement: The merge driver MUST check the merged file against its table's own rules (fields, types, keys and checks) and fail on a record that breaks them; keys to other tables MUST be checked when the data next loads.

title: Git runs the driver for every data file
statement: Git MUST run the merge driver for every data file, writing the merge over ours as git expects.

title: A driver that cannot start says the file was not merged
statement: When the merge driver cannot start because its lathe is not installed, it MUST fail the merge with one message that names the missing package, says the file was not merged and holds only our side, and gives the command to install and the command to merge the file again.

title: A business outcome sits under its product and is measurable
statement: A business outcome MUST sit under its product and give a statement of the outcome, its measure and its target; the store MUST refuse one that leaves any of them out.

title: Discovery is the first stage, holding outcomes and journeys
statement: Discovery MUST be the first stage, before the domain model, and hold the business outcomes and the journeys that reach them, which follow the product in the kinds' order.

title: Tests and the product's own records measure outcomes
statement: A business outcome MAY be measured by any number of tests of any kind, each a measured_by link from the outcome, and a test MAY measure several outcomes. A record of a product's own kind (a report, a script, a check) MAY measure one only once the product allows that kind with a product_relation named measured_by; no other kind of Lathe's measures. An outcome that nothing in the code can measure MAY say instead how it is measured outside the code.

title: A product's interfaces each have a kind, roles and use cases
statement: Each interface of a product MUST have one kind (web, desktop, API, command line, agent tools or other), the roles of the product that use it and the use cases it offers, and MUST go with its roles and offers, refused while referenced.

title: A journey runs from a trigger to a result, under its product
statement: A journey MUST sit under its product and give its trigger, what starts it in the world, and its result, what it ends in; the store MUST refuse one that leaves either out.

title: A step carries out a use case or a handoff of its product
statement: Each step of a journey MAY carry out one use case of any domain of the journey's product, or one of its policies as a handoff, and MUST carry out nothing of another product; a step that carries out nothing yet MUST be allowed, and is reported as a use case still to write.

title: A journey's steps are in order on each path
statement: A journey's steps MUST be in order on its main path and on each alternate path, every path numbered 1, 2, 3 without gaps, and moving a step MUST keep every path so numbered.

title: A journey serves outcomes beside the capabilities
statement: A journey MAY serve any number of its product's business outcomes, each a serves link from the journey, beside the capabilities that serve them; the use cases and policies its steps carry out MUST then serve those outcomes through it.

title: A journey has at most one journey test
statement: A journey MAY have one journey test, which drives its main path end to end from its trigger to its result at the service, system or browser level, and MUST NOT have two.

title: What a step carries out cannot be removed under it
statement: Removing a use case or policy a journey step carries out MUST be refused, naming the step, until the step is removed or linked to another; removing a journey MUST remove its steps and its test, never what they carry out.

title: A journey of fewer than two use cases is warned
statement: A journey whose steps carry out fewer than two use cases MUST be warned of as a use case, not a journey.

title: A handoff its previous use case does not lead to is warned
statement: A handoff step whose policy hears no event raised by a command that the flow of the use case step before it invokes MUST be warned of, once that use case has a flow.

title: An outcome timing a duration that no journey serves is warned
statement: A business outcome whose measure reads as a duration, such as the days from one thing to another, MUST be warned of while no journey serves it, saying to write the journey it times.

title: A record of a product's own kind is held to its declaration
statement: A record of a product's own kind MUST be added, changed and removed only through the Extension record's commands, each held to its kind's declared fields and relations, and MUST go with its links and packages, refused while anything references it.

title: A product names the roles its use cases name
statement: A product MUST list the roles its use cases and interfaces name, each with a description of the part it plays.

title: An open question sits where it is asked
statement: An open question MUST sit under its product or one of its domains and MAY be about any records of its product; a decided question is removed with its links, its answer written into the records it affects.

title: Each record's product and domain come from its parents
statement: The engine MUST give each record its product and domain from its Parent fields, through the store's record scope. Data the store refuses, such as a cycle of parents, MUST make the load end with one data-refused error per refusal, naming the file, line and rule, and no records, rather than loop or load in part.

title: A record with no owner belongs to the one domain that uses it
statement: The store's record scope MUST give a view, an integration, an interface part and a value object the domain that uses it, worked out from the links and fields and never stored: a view the domains of the commands and queries it presents; an integration those whose flow steps or policies exchange with it; an interface part those that use the views it renders; a value object those of the entities, domain events and read models whose fields it types. When exactly one domain uses the record, that is its domain; when two or more do, or none, it has no domain and the product shares it. What sits under it (constraints, view requirements, their tests, the technical records of a value object, a connector to an outside system, integration tests) MUST follow it. A specification keeps the domain its ID names. IDs stay product-scoped, so a record that gains or loses a using domain moves with no rename and no change to the data. Every check, coverage report and the Workbench MUST read this one answer.

title: An unknown parent is refused once
statement: A record whose Parent field names no record MUST be refused once, as a foreign key naming the missing record and the kind it must be, and nothing else MAY be reported about that Parent.

title: An ID is used once
statement: An ID MUST be used by one record only, of any kind, in any product the store loads, so that an ID cited on its own (in a test name, a code file, a command or an address in the Workbench) means exactly one record. A record that takes an ID in use MUST be refused once, as unique-id, naming the record that has it with its file and line, and the links to that ID MUST NOT be refused with it.

title: An ID fits its scope
statement: A record's ID MUST start with its parent's ID, its domain's ID or its product's ID and a hyphen, as its kind's ID scope says; a record with no owner starts with a product's ID, and a specification with a domain's.

title: A link or parent the schema does not allow is refused once
statement: The store MUST refuse a link between two kinds its relation does not allow, naming the kinds that end accepts, and a Parent field its kind does not have, each once.

title: Linked records share a product
statement: Every link, and every field typed by a value object or an aggregate, MUST join two records of the same product; an ID of another product in text is plain text, never a link.

title: An ID in text is kept as written and makes no link
statement: The engine MUST keep a record's text exactly as written, IDs, repeats, its own ID, code spans and fences included, and MUST NOT read a link, a mention or any other relation from it. Only a Link relates two records.

title: No check reads text for IDs
statement: Checks MUST NOT report an ID in text, whether a record has it or not and whatever its prefix; the engine's one problem of its own is `data-refused`.

title: Each record is one entry of its kind, one line of its file
statement: Each record MUST be one entry of its kind, with typed fields, kept as one line of its kind's data file; its parts and its links MUST be entries of their own. The data files MUST be the source of truth: nothing else MAY hold a record's content, and the store built from them is never committed.

title: Line and field order do not change what a data file means
statement: Reordering the lines of a data file, or the fields of a line, MUST NOT change what the data means: a record's product, domain, parent and links come only from its fields, its ID and its relations' entries. A file in the data folder that is not a data file in Lathe's format MUST be ignored.

title: Standards, their tests and meets are in the schema
statement:
The schema MUST have a `standard` kind under the product and a `standard_rule` kind under a standard, in the technical specification stage, with IDs `

-STD-` and `-R`; a `standard_rule_test` kind under a standard rule, in the test plan stage, with IDs `-T`, any number per rule, at any level; and the relation `meets` from a technical record to a standard rule, labeled Meets and Met by, with no role. The reference MUST describe them.

title: A standard rule is owed, met by technical records and proved by its tests
statement: A standard rule MUST be an obligation of the product: designed and built by the technical records that meet it, and proved by its standard rule tests, automated or manual, whose file names them. One that nothing meets MUST be reported as not designed, and one with no such test as not proved.

title: Each technical record sits under the record it builds and names its file
statement: Each technical record MUST sit under the record it builds, as its kind says: a data model and a table under an entity, a read model or its domain; a projection under a read model; a command handler under a command; a query handler under a query; an event handler under a policy; an event type under an event; a value type under a value object; a predicate under a specification; an endpoint handler under an endpoint; an adapter under an integration; a repository, a service and a UI component under their domain. It MAY name its file, relative to the repo root; a file that does not exist yet is work still to do.

title: A table stores only what fields can't say
statement: A table's stored fields MUST follow from its entity's or read model's fields, with value objects flattened; the table MUST store its name, its storage and its keys, and a unique key MAY name the invariant it enforces.

title: A record can point at the code that builds or proves it
statement: A technical record MUST be able to name its `file`, and a test its run by's `file` that runs it, each as a path relative to the repo root.

title: An entry point names the file that starts it
statement: An entry point MUST sit under its domain, be titled by its identifier exactly as in code, and name the file that starts the product or one of its processes.

title: Tooling names its script or configuration
statement: A tooling record MUST sit under its domain, be titled by its identifier exactly as in code, and name the script or configuration file that builds, checks or tests the product.

title: Every repository, reader and table names its one data store
statement: The schema MUST have `data_store`, under a product or one of its domains, with its kind, and the relations `stored_in` (each repository, reader or table to at most one data store) and `provided_by` (a data store to at most one integration); coverage MUST report a repository, reader or table that names no data store, and a data store nothing is kept in.

title: Coverage counts designed and proved obligations
statement: For each domain, coverage MUST give the number of obligations of each obligation kind, and how many of each are designed and how many are proved. Built counts are LA-TRC-UC01-R04; not-automated-yet counts are LA-TRC-UC02-R03.

title: Coverage lists each gap with what it lacks
statement: Coverage MUST list each obligation that is not designed, not built or not proved, with its kind, saying which it lacks, and the `not-designed`, `not-built` and `not-proved` warnings MUST name exactly the obligations coverage counts as lacking it.

title: Coverage gaps are warnings, not errors
statement: A gap MUST be reported as a warning, so that an honest, unfinished design still passes `lathe check`.

title: Coverage reports built separately from designed
statement: For each domain, coverage MUST give how many obligations of each kind are built: every technical record that implements its design names a file that exists, and there is at least one. The built count MUST never be more than the designed count, so a domain whose code does not exist yet shows as designed but not built.

title: Coverage lists each record short of a minimum as a gap named by its rule
statement: Coverage MUST list, under the record's own scope, each record short of a minimum the schema leaves to coverage (an aggregate with no root, a use case with no flow, an entity with no storage of its own unless it is stored with its root, and the rest of the gap rules), as a gap named by its rule, never as a problem. Each gap rule MUST have a unique name, a stage and a one-sentence summary.

title: The Reader sees how complete each domain is and what is undecided or broken
statement: Opening a product, the Reader MUST see each domain with how much of it is designed, built and proved, and the product's open questions and problems, without running anything.

title: Coverage counts every obligation kind
