statement: For each domain, coverage MUST give one entry per obligation kind (constraint, invariant, specification, policy, domain service, UC requirement, view requirement, API requirement, pattern rule, standard rule, and every product kind declared an obligation), in schema order, even when the domain has none of that kind. Each entry MUST give the total and how many are designed, built, proved and not automated yet.

title: Designed, built and proved follow from the tree
statement: An obligation MUST count as designed when its design is specified, as built when every one of the specific technical records that implement that design names a file that exists (and there is at least one), and as proved when a test under it is automated or manual, at a level its kind allows. A UC requirement is designed when a flow step of its use case fulfills it, and built when every record that carries out its fulfilling steps names a file that exists: the record that handles each command or query a step invokes, with the predicates of the specifications and the services of the domain services that command or query checks, selects by or calls, and the connector of each integration a step exchanges with (LA-TRC-UC02-R10); an interface part of the view a step happens in does not build it. Any other obligation is designed when the technical record of its kind exists, and built when every such record names a file that exists: a constraint's technical record (of its value object), an invariant's rule, a specification's predicate, a policy's event handling, a domain service's service, a view requirement's interface parts that build it, an API requirement's handling record (of its operation). A product relation declared with the design, build or proof role counts as design, build or proof of its target. Coverage is counted in the domain the obligation belongs to.

title: A test not automated yet makes an obligation not automated yet, not proved
statement: An obligation MUST count as proved only when an automated or manual test proves it, and as not automated yet when it is not proved but a test not automated yet is meant to prove it. The `not-proved` warning for such an obligation SHOULD say that its test is not automated yet.

title: The check prints one coverage line per domain and obligation kind
statement: `lathe check` MUST print one coverage line for each domain and obligation kind the domain has, with designed, built, proved and not-automated-yet counts out of the total and the number of gaps; a domain with no obligations gets one line saying so.

title: Each obligation kind says when it is built
statement: Coverage MUST count an obligation as built only through the specific code that builds it, by its kind, never through other code near it: an invariant when its rule names its file, a UC requirement when a step that fulfills it invokes a command or query whose handling record names its file, a view requirement when an interface part that builds it names its file (not one that only renders its view), an API requirement when the record that handles its operation names its file, a standard rule when a technical record that meets it names its file. A product's own obligation kind is built by the sources of the links its declaration gives the design or build role.

title: Proof counts only at a level the test's kind allows
statement: A test MUST count as proof only when its run by level is one its kind allows (LA-TRC-DS02); at another level it counts as nothing, and LA-CHK-UC01-R09 reports it.

title: A constraint counts in its value object's domain, or in Shared
statement: A constraint MUST count in the coverage of the domain its value object belongs to (`LA-PRD-UC37-R02`): the one domain whose entities, events or read models have fields typed by it. The constraint of a value object two or more domains use, or none, MUST count once, in the product's Shared coverage, and its one test proves it there.

title: A product proof that names a file is named in it
statement: A record of a product kind that a proof link names, and that names a file, MUST count as proof only when that file exists and names the record's ID, as a test's file must, and a record that names no file MUST count as it stands.

title: An integration's connector that carries out a step builds what the step fulfills
statement: A UC requirement MUST also count as built when a flow step that fulfills it exchanges with an integration whose connector names a file that exists: the connector carries the step out. A record of a product's own kind under that integration does not build it. This holds for every product.

title: An outcome nothing serves, and a capability that serves none, are gaps
statement: Coverage MUST report as gaps a business outcome no capability serves, under the product outside every domain, and a capability that serves no business outcome, under its domain; neither is a problem.

title: A source file no technical record names is a gap
statement: Coverage MUST report as a code-file-untraced gap, under the product outside every domain, each source file (the source patterns in the product's configuration, defaulting to code in the common languages) that no technical record names, directly or through a folder it names; tests (the test patterns and files in test folders), configurations, generated files and build output MUST be left out. Code MUST NOT need to carry record IDs for this.

title: An outcome nothing measures is a gap
statement: Coverage MUST report as a gap, under the product outside every domain, a business outcome that names no measure outside the code and that no record of a product's own kind and no test that runs measures: a test not automated yet, or an automated one whose file is missing or does not name it, measures nothing. It is never a problem.

title: A product's relation with a role counts on Lathe's obligation kinds too
statement: A relation a product declares with a role MUST count toward coverage for every obligation it links to, Lathe's own kinds included: a design link designs the obligation, a build link builds it when its source names a file that exists, and a proof link proves it as the product's own obligation kinds are proved; a design link on one of Lathe's kinds MUST NOT build it, since the kind says what builds it.

title: An integration's connector builds a policy that exchanges with it
statement: A policy that exchanges with an integration MUST count as built only when the code that carries the policy out and that integration's connector each name a file that exists: the connector carries out the policy's exchange. This holds for every product.

title: A pattern rule is an obligation under a pattern
statement: A pattern rule record MUST sit under a pattern and MUST be an obligation counted for proof alone (LA-TRC-UC07-R05), proved in each domain by a pattern rule test under it that names the domain, at most one per rule and domain. It MAY name, in its setting field, the one pattern setting it depends on.

title: Each domain that follows a pattern owes its rules
statement: Coverage MUST count each pattern rule once in each domain that owes it (LA-TRC-SP04), on that domain's `pattern_rule` line. A domain that does not follow the pattern MUST NOT count the rule, and the rule's gaps MUST name it in each domain that owes it.

title: A domain's own pattern rule test proves a pattern rule there
statement: In each domain that owes a pattern rule, the rule MUST count as proved only when its pattern rule test naming that domain is automated or manual, and as not automated yet when that test is not automated yet. One domain's test MUST NOT count for another.

title: Not-proved warnings name the pattern rule and the domain
statement: The `not-proved` warning MUST report a pattern rule once for each domain that owes it and lacks the proof, with a message naming the rule and the domain, such as "Pattern rule TL-PAT-LIBRARIAN-ACTION-R01 is not proved in TL-LEND", and MUST say when its test there is not automated yet.

title: A pattern that no use case or domain follows is a warning
statement: When no use case and no domain follows a pattern, the engine MUST report a `pattern-not-followed` warning on the pattern, saying how many of its rules are therefore not counted in any domain.

title: An obligation outside every domain counts in Shared
statement: An obligation that sits in no domain, such as a product's own obligation kind declared under the product, MUST count in its product's Shared coverage, so every obligation is counted somewhere. Pattern rules are counted in the domains that owe them (LA-TRC-UC04-R02) and never in Shared.

title: An automated test's file names the test's ID
statement: An automated test's `file` MUST name the test's own ID, matched only as a whole ID (LA-TRC-DS01). Otherwise the engine MUST report a `test-file-missing-id` error naming the test and the file, and the test MUST NOT count as proof.

title: A manual or not-yet-automated test's file is checked only for existing
statement: The engine MUST NOT report `test-file-missing-id` for a manual test or a test not automated yet; a file it names is checked only for existing.

title: A product proof's file is checked as a test's
statement: A record of a product kind that a proof link names, and that names a file, MUST be checked as an automated test is: the engine MUST report a test-file-missing error when the file does not exist, and a test-file-missing-id error when it does not name the record's ID. A record of a product kind that names a file but proves nothing MUST NOT be reported by either check.

title: Every test case in the code names the test it proves
statement: The engine MUST read the product's test files (the files matching the test patterns in the product's configuration, by default the common test and spec file names, never in node_modules, dist or another product's folder, and every file a test record names) and find each test case in them: a call of it or test, with its modifiers and each forms, whose name is a string or template literal, inheriting the names of the describe calls around it. A test case whose name, describes' names and each entries name no ID of a test whose file is the file it is in (or of a product kind's record that proves an obligation) MUST be reported as a test-case-unnamed error naming the file, line and test case.

title: Coverage counts each domain's tests by state
statement: Each domain's coverage MUST report `tests`: how many tests sit in the domain with each state, automated, manual and not automated yet, each test counted once, in the domain its parent belongs to (a pattern rule test in the domain it names). A domain with no tests MUST report zero of each.

title: lathe check reports each domain's tests by state
statement: After a domain's obligation lines, `lathe check`'s coverage report MUST print one line with its tests by state, such as `LA-CHK tests: 50 automated, 0 manual, 7 not automated yet`.

title: The Reader sees each domain's tests by state beside its coverage
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read a product's and each domain's tests by state, automated, manual and not automated yet, beside its coverage, totaled in the product's summary.

title: A domain may follow a pattern and then owes every rule
statement: A `domain` MAY follow a pattern with the `follows` relation. Coverage MUST then count each of the pattern's rules in that domain.

title: A domain follows a pattern itself or through any of its use cases
statement: Coverage and its warnings MUST treat a domain as following a pattern when the domain or any of its use cases follows it (LA-TRC-SP01), and MUST count each rule once there.

title: A pattern may have no settings
statement: A pattern MAY have no settings. A rule with no setting MUST apply wherever its pattern is followed, and pattern-setting-missing MUST ask only for the settings a pattern has.

title: A product's own kind may be an obligation
statement: A product kind MAY be declared an obligation (`product_kind.obligation`), and coverage MUST then count it as any other obligation kind.

title: A pattern rule is counted for proof alone
statement: For pattern rules, coverage MUST report designed and built as equal to the total and give no design or build gaps, and the `not-designed` and `not-built` warnings MUST NOT fire. Proved, not-automated-yet and proof gaps MUST work as for any obligation.

title: Pattern rules need proof only, and a product cannot widen them
statement: Lathe MUST refuse a product kind that takes the name of one of Lathe's own kinds of record, so a pattern rule asks for proof alone in every domain that owes it.

title: A use case that follows a pattern is not asked for requirements
statement: The `use-case-without-requirements` warning MUST NOT fire for a use case that follows a pattern.

title: A pattern rule test outside its pattern's followers is an error
statement: A pattern rule test naming a domain that does not follow its rule's pattern MUST be a `pattern-rule-test-outside-followers` error naming the test, the rule, the domain and the pattern.

title: A manual test whose file never mentions it is reported
statement: A manual test whose `file` exists but does not name the test's ID MUST get a `manual-test-file-silent` warning naming the test and the file. Automated tests and tests not automated yet MUST NOT get this warning.

title: The Reader reads one requirement's path
statement: On a UC requirement the Reader MUST be able to select it in its use case's line on the Trace stage and read its path: the steps that fulfill it, their technical chain and the tests that prove it, with any gap showing at once.

title: The Trace stage shows the engine's chains and gaps
statement: Each obligation's chain MUST be the engine's, worked out with coverage by the relations it counts: what designs it, what builds it as built counts it, its tests and the files they name. An obligation's gaps MUST be the ones coverage reports, and a flow step, command, query or interface part no obligation's chain reaches MUST be a record-untraced coverage gap, so every interface of Lathe reports the same records. The Trace stage MUST NOT work any of it out itself.

title: The Reader follows each use case from its outcome to its tests
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read each use case of a product once, from the business outcomes its capability serves through its requirements, its flow's steps, each interface's version of them and their technical chain to its acceptance tests, with how far each stage has come (designed, built, proved), from the Trace read model.

title: The Reader reads coverage for every obligation kind and every test state
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read, for every obligation kind the model names, how much is designed, built and proved, and tell at a glance which tests are automated, manual or not automated yet.

title: The Reader sees which pattern rules a domain owes and whether it proves each
statement: Opening a domain, the Reader MUST see the patterns it follows and, for each rule, whether the domain proves it.

title: The Reader sees what designs, builds and proves an obligation
statement: Opening an obligation, the Reader MUST see below its text what designs it, whether that is built, and the tests under it with their states, each gap called out.

title: A use case shows its requirements designed, built and proved
statement: A use case's Traceability MUST show its requirements with Designed, Built and Proved for each.

title: A technical record shows what it builds and that record's tests
statement: A technical record's Traceability MUST show the obligations it builds and the tests that prove them, each with its state.

title: A test shows what it proves and its run by
statement: A test's Traceability MUST show the obligation it proves and its run by: its level, its state and its file.

title: An operation's file names its method and address
statement: The file of the record that handles an operation MUST name the operation's address, compared in the address normal form (LA-TRC-DS04) and found in code, a string or a comment, with the operation's method written in capitals or called as .post( on the address's line or within two lines of it. Otherwise the engine MUST report an error naming the operation, its method and address, and the file. A record whose file does not exist yet MUST NOT be reported here.

title: A view's address is named in a file of an interface part that renders it
statement: When a view has an address, a file of one of the interface parts that render it MUST name that address, compared in the address normal form (LA-TRC-DS04). Otherwise the engine MUST report an error naming the view, its address and the files it read. A view with no address, or none of whose interface parts' files exists, MUST NOT be reported.

title: Every address the code serves has an operation or a view
statement: The engine MUST read the files of the records that handle the product's operations, and the router files the product's configuration names (glob patterns from the root), for the addresses their code serves: an address literal passed to a method call such as app.get('/tools'), given as a path, pattern or address key or attribute, compared with ===, ==, !== or !=, or assigned to a constant whose name marks it as a path; never one in a comment. A served address that no operation of its method has, and that no view has when it is served for GET or any method, both compared in the address normal form (LA-TRC-DS04), MUST be a coverage gap of the product naming the method, address, file and line.

title: A stored kind's file defines its name, fields and keys
statement: For each entity or read model kept in its own storage that names a file that exists, the engine MUST read that file as text and report a schema-mismatch warning for each part it does not define: the stored kind by its name, each field its entity's or read model's fields give, and each primary, unique and foreign key by its fields, a foreign key also by the stored kind it targets.

title: A stored field's name follows from the field
statement: A field's stored name MUST be the stored name it is given when it gives one, else its name in lower case with every run of other characters an underscore. A field typed by a value object of several fields MUST be flattened into that value object's fields, and an entity's storage MUST also hold the fields of the children kept with its root.

title: A stored kind with no file is a gap
statement: A kind of record kept in its own storage that names no file MUST be reported as a coverage gap.

title: Every package a manifest lists is named by a record
statement: Each package that one of the product's package manifests lists under dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies or peerDependencies MUST be named by a package use of a technical record of the product. Coverage MUST report the packages no record names as one package-not-accounted-for gap on the product, naming each package with the manifests that list it.

title: A record names only a package a manifest lists
statement: A record whose package use names a package that none of its product's package manifests lists MUST be reported by a package-not-in-manifest error naming the record and the package.

title: Only a technical record names a package
statement: Lathe MUST refuse a package use on a record whose kind is not in the technical specification (package-use-technical), Lathe's kinds and a product's own alike, and a package name that is not one npm allows.

title: The manifests are those of the package folders
statement: The manifests MUST be the package manifest of each folder the product's configuration lists as packages, or, when it lists none, of the root and of each folder directly under it (not hidden, not node_modules) that holds one. A listed folder outside the root, or with no package manifest, MUST stop the load with a message naming it.

title: Each record names the outcomes it serves
statement: Each record MUST name the business outcomes it serves, worked out on every read from the use cases whose capability serves an outcome, or that a step of a journey serving it carries out, and the policies such a journey hands off through, that reach it (LA-TRC-DS06), never stored or typed in: shown on the record as its Serves line, each outcome a link and marked with the journey it is served through, and available through any of Lathe's interfaces as get-serves and list-serves.

title: What no outcome reaches is reported
statement: An aggregate, read model or obligation no outcome reaches MUST be reported by a serves-no-outcome warning that says to write the use case that needs it or remove it, and MUST be listed by list-serves as serving none.

title: A fill of a record that tooling generates is refused
statement: A fill of a record that a tooling record generates MUST be refused, giving every reason and changing nothing: generated records are accounted for already.

title: A journey's proof is rolled up from its steps and its test
statement: A journey MUST read as proved only when its journey test counts and every step is proved, a use case step when its UC requirements and its flow test are and a handoff when its policy's test is; the roll-up MUST be worked out from the records on every read, never stored, and read the same through any of Lathe's interfaces.

title: A journey's proof shows where its outcomes and use cases are traced
statement: A journey's proof MUST be shown with the journey, with each outcome it serves and in the product's trace between the outcomes and the use cases its steps carry out, and each use case MUST show in its trace the journeys it is a step of.

title: Each journey gap is reported with what to write
statement: A journey without a journey test, with no step on its main path, or serving no outcome, and a step that carries out nothing yet, MUST each be reported as a coverage gap that says what to write.

title: A record has at most one provider
statement: A record MUST have at most one provider; naming another MUST replace the one it had.

title: Every test gives its run by
statement: Every test MUST give its run by: a level, a state, and a file when it is automated or a manual reason when it is manual. Its file MUST name the test's ID, as LA-TRC-UC05 sets out.

title: A test's state is automated, manual or not automated yet
statement: A test's `state` MUST be one of `automated`, `manual` and `not automated yet`, and every test MUST give one: the store MUST refuse any other value, or none. The checks and coverage MUST read it the same way.

title: Only an automated test needs a file, and only a manual test gives a reason
statement: The store MUST refuse an automated test with no `file`, a manual test with no `manual_reason`, and a manual reason on any other test. A test not automated yet MAY name the file it will live in before that file exists; that MUST be a warning, not an error. Any other file a test names MUST exist (`test-file-missing`, an error).

title: A test's level is one of five
statement: A test's `level` MUST be one of unit, integration, service, system and browser, and the store MUST refuse any other value, or none.

title: A test gives its size and markers
statement: A test's run by MAY give its size, volume or worst case, and is small when it gives none; it MAY mark itself smoke or external, each only as yes, and the store MUST refuse small and a marker of no, which are written by leaving them out.

title: Tests start from test data sets
statement: A test data set MUST sit under a domain and MAY give the environment, accounts and starting records some tests need, how to prepare and reset them, and the seed or fixture file that builds them; any kind of test MAY start from any number of them, each a starts_from link.

title: A data set nothing uses, or whose file is missing, is reported
statement: A test data set no test starts from MUST be reported as an error, and one whose file does not exist MUST be reported: as an error when an automated test starts from it, else as a warning.

title: A pattern sits under the product and use cases or domains follow it
statement: A pattern MUST sit under a product and MAY list its settings. A use case, or a domain, MAY follow one or more patterns with the `follows` relation.

title: A pattern rule is owed by every domain that follows it, and proved per domain
statement: A pattern rule MUST be an obligation of each domain that follows its pattern, or has a use case that does, proved by one pattern rule test per rule and domain.

title: A use case has one flow, whose steps reach operations
statement: The schema MUST have an `interface` under each product, of kind web, API, command line, agent tools, desktop or other, that MAY offer the product's use cases, and at most one `flow` per use case, with `flow_step` under it with a required `position` and `path`; a step MAY fulfill its use case's requirements, invoke a command or query, exchange with integrations and name the one interface it is a variant of.

title: A requirement a flow misses is a gap
statement: A UC requirement that no step of its use case's flow fulfills MUST be reported as not designed, naming the flow.

title: A flow's ID is its use case's and FL
statement: A flow's ID MUST be its use case's ID and FL (TL-LEND-UC01-FL); `next-id` MUST give it, and refuse a use case that already has its flow.

title: Every interface that offers a use case reaches its steps
statement: A step that invokes a command or query MUST be reached by every interface that offers its use case, but for another interface's variant: an app a person works in by a view that presents it, calls other programs make by the call that exposes it, a command line or agent tools by a record of the product's own interaction design kinds under it or that presents it (one that sits under an interface for that interface only, any other for every command line and agent tools of the product, as a view of every such interface or of one); one that is not MUST be warned of (step-unreached). A variant of an interface that does not offer its use case MUST be an error (variant-not-offered); a flow no interface offers, and an interface that offers a use case none of whose actors it lists among its roles, MUST be warned of (flow-not-offered, interface-actor-not-the-use-case).

title: Each interface's version of a flow is derived, never stored
statement: Each interface that offers a use case MUST have its own version of the use case's flow, worked out from the steps and never stored: its actor (the first of the use case's actors it lists), the patterns it follows and their rules, and its steps without the other interfaces' variants, each with where it is carried out.

title: An interface that offers no use case is a gap
statement: An interface that offers no use case MUST be reported as a gap (interface-offers-nothing).

title: Each use case command changes one use case, held to its rules
statement: Each command of the Use case aggregate MUST load the use case it changes whole through its repository, hold it to the aggregate's rules before it saves, and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file.

title: A record of a use case goes with what it holds, refused while referenced
statement: Removing a use case, or a requirement, flow, step or test in one, MUST take what sits under it and the links they start, and MUST be refused, naming what does, while anything left still references them.

title: A use case with no flow is a coverage gap, never an error
statement: A use case with no flow MUST be reported in its domain's coverage as a `use-case-without-flow` gap, a record short of a minimum. It MUST NOT be an error, so `lathe check` does not fail because of it.

title: Requirements and rules may name a group
statement: A `uc_requirement`, `view_requirement`, `api_requirement`, `pattern_rule` or `standard_rule` MAY name a short heading in `group_name`, such as Validation or Paging, so that a long list of them is sorted under headings as a real product sorts it. A group is a field, not a record, so renaming one MUST change no ID.

title: A use case under a capability belongs to the capability's domain
statement: A use case, and everything under it, MUST belong to the capability's domain, so that its obligations count in that domain's coverage exactly as they did directly under the domain. A use case moved under another domain's capability takes that domain's IDs (LA-MOD-UC02-R09).

title: A path whose positions skip a number is a step-order error
statement: The steps on each path of a flow SHOULD run 1, 2, 3 without a gap, the path compared trimmed and in any letter case. A path whose positions skip a number MUST be reported once as a `step-order` error, on the first step after the gap.

title: A requirement moved to another use case takes that use case's next number
statement: Moving a UC requirement to another use case of its product MUST give it the next free number under that use case, and its tests the new requirement's ID in place of the old one's, and MUST carry each new ID into every record that names the old one. A requirement a step of its own use case still fulfills MUST be refused until the step no longer does.
